skill.name: agent-transit
skill.description: Visualize one local Claude Code, Codex CLI, or Cursor session as an interactive subway map of tool calls.
skill.summary: Create local session maps with tool families, timing, slow calls, and error markers.
skill.author: israelvicars

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are false positives from JavaScript syntax, regular expressions, synthetic fixtures, or expected local tooling. Confirmed issues include optional contract HTML injection, plaintext credential transport, and strict-sharing privacy gaps. No evidence found of malicious intent; 278 unpresented static matches still require manual review before automatic publication. Static review was capped at 400/678 representative findings; omitted static matches are unconfirmed, so automatic publishing stays disabled until manual review.

remediation.suggestion: Manually review the omitted 278 static analyzer matches or reduce bundled generated/vendor/reference content before enabling automatic publication.

remediation.issue: Optional contract confidence values reach panel.innerHTML without escaping.
remediation.suggestion: Validate contract indexes, restrict confidence to known enum values, and escape every dynamic field before HTML insertion.

remediation.issue: Optional PostHog and Tempo adapters can transmit credentials over HTTP.
remediation.suggestion: Require HTTPS whenever credentials are present. Allow local HTTP only through an explicit, narrowly scoped override with a warning.

remediation.issue: Search argument fragments appear in default shared tool labels.
remediation.suggestion: Omit query, pattern, and URL fragments by default. Add separate consent for target previews and regression tests with confidential query terms.

remediation.issue: Strict sharing preserves arbitrary internal trace fields and nested event payloads.
remediation.suggestion: Construct a fresh allowlisted export object. Drop unknown metadata and fields, recursively scrub retained values, and test nested payload canaries.

remediation.issue: The static catalog excludes 278 repeated or lower-priority matches.
remediation.suggestion: Complete manual review of the omitted matches before enabling automatic publication. Preserve this review limitation in the publication decision.

content.user_title: Visualize Coding Agent Sessions as Transit Maps
content.value_statement: Coding session logs make tool sequences and delays difficult to review. Agent Transit turns one local session into an interactive map with timing and failure markers.
actual_capabilities: Convert one Claude Code, Codex CLI, or Cursor session into a self-contained interactive HTML map.
Group tool calls by family and mark slow calls, errors, and permission denials.
Build strict-share pages with additional scrubbing and an initial selection on the first failing call.
Shorten idle gaps while retaining wall-time metadata and an option for original timing.
Export one Cursor composer from read-only SQLite storage into reduced metadata JSONL.
Render GIF, MP4, and contact-sheet outputs, then verify repeated frames, departure timing, and blank-frame checks.
limitations: Redaction does not guarantee confidentiality; query fragments and extra internal trace fields can survive strict sharing.
Cursor support is experimental; call end times are estimates, and older transcripts use synthetic durations.
Node.js 20 or later is required; the Cursor exporter needs sqlite3 or Node.js 22.5 or later.
Video export requires Chromium and ffmpeg; first-run setup may download missing dependencies and a browser.

best_practices: Keep original sessions local and inspect every generated artifact for confidential labels before sharing.
Use strict sharing, leave argument previews disabled, and treat scrubbing as partial protection.
Start with synthetic fixtures and approve dependency downloads before rendering sensitive sessions.
anti_patterns: Treating strict-share output as guaranteed free of confidential data.
Interpreting estimated or synthetic Cursor durations as exact execution times.
Sharing original logs or enabling argument previews without reviewing retained data.

faq.question: Which coding agents are supported?
faq.answer: The adapters support Claude Code, Codex CLI, and experimental Cursor session formats.

faq.question: Does session data leave my machine?
faq.answer: HTML generation is local. Rendering setup may download dependencies, and optional request-trace adapters contact configured services. Uploads require a separate sharing action.

faq.question: Does strict sharing remove every secret?
faq.answer: No. It adds scrubbing, but query fragments and extra internal trace fields can remain. Review output before sharing.

faq.question: What software is required?
faq.answer: HTML builds require Node.js 20 or later. Video rendering also requires Chromium and ffmpeg; setup may download missing components.

faq.question: How accurate is Cursor timing?
faq.answer: Newer bubbles provide start timestamps, but end times use the next message as an upper bound. Older transcripts use uniform synthetic durations.

faq.question: Can I export animations and check their rendering?
faq.answer: The bundled scripts produce GIF, MP4, and contact sheets. Verification compares repeated frames and checks departure timing and blank frames.
